question: Yesterday your support agent ran a named session on a customer's billing dispute and called get_customer and lookup_order. Overnight, the billing team reversed one charge, and the customer changed the account's payment method. Several of those tool results no longer match the backend. You plan to start a new session with a structured summary of yesterday's findings instead of resuming the old one. Which reason best explains why this plan is more reliable?

options.text: Resuming a session discards the earlier tool results automatically, so the agent would lose yesterday's findings and repeat the whole investigation.
options.reason: Wrong. Resumption continues the prior conversation with its context intact. The problem is that the stale tool results persist, not that they are lost.

options.text: Session resumption is unreliable for any customer conversation, so prior context from a support session should never be carried into later work.
options.reason: Wrong. The guide says to choose resumption when the prior context is mostly valid. A fresh start with a summary is preferred only when prior tool results are stale.

options.text: A resumed session cannot call get_customer or lookup_order again, so the agent would be unable to fetch the corrected account and order data.
options.reason: Wrong. The guide describes telling a resumed session about specific changes so that it can do targeted re-analysis. Tools stay usable after resumption; the risk is that stale results remain in context.

options.text: A resumed session keeps the old tool results in its context, so the agent may reason from outdated charges and payment details as if they were current.
options.reason: Correct. The resumed context still holds the stale tool results. A fresh session with a structured summary carries forward only the still-valid findings and flags what must be fetched again.
